bib.title: AI Systems Performance Engineering, Chapter 13. Profiling, Tuning, and Scaling PyTorch
bib.venue: O'Reilly (book chapter; author and year not printed in the PDF text, taken from the repo's notes)

question: How do you profile PyTorch training and inference at every layer of the stack (Python, CPU, kernels, memory, multi-GPU) and apply targeted tuning (torch.compile, CUDA streams and graphs, allocator, FSDP/DDP, data pipeline) while guarding against regressions?
contributions: A profile-first workflow with PyTorch profiler, NVTX, Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, Linux perf, HTA and Perfetto on an MoE example
torch.compile modes, regional compilation and graph-break debugging
CUDA streams, CUDA Graphs and CUDA Graph Trees in PyTorch
Memory tuning (allocator, activation checkpointing, offload, FSDP) and data-pipeline tuning
CI performance-regression testing, PyTorch HUD and MLPerf-style logging

limits: Numbers (profile tables, 248 vs 173 ms, roofline before/after, perf output, MLPerf breakdown) come from one illustrative MoE example with no model size, GPU model, batch or run counts beyond batch size 4; the perf stat output has round, likely illustrative counters.
The text says max-autotune produced the 173 ms result but the printed code compiles with reduce-overhead; one of the two is wrong.
No repeated runs, variance or seeds are reported for any measurement.
Advice on DDP bucket size conflicts within the chapter (bigger buckets launch earlier vs one giant bucket loses overlap).
Recommends torch.utils.data DataPipes, and the CUDA-stream-per-request pattern for inference serving; both are shaky or dated.

practices: Profile first at several layers (PyTorch profiler, Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, perf) and optimise one change at a time, measuring each (Profiling PyTorch; perf section).
Mark phases with NVTX and record_function so tools can correlate (NVTX Markers section).
Use torch.compile first, custom kernels only for what the compiler misses (Compiling Versus Writing Custom Kernels).
Start with the default compile mode; try reduce-overhead or max-autotune and measure; for dynamic token routing prefer default or max-autotune-no-cudagraphs (Compilation Modes).
Use regional compilation for repeated transformer blocks to cut cold-start time (Regional Compilation).
Cache compiled artifacts (save_cache_artifacts, TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR) across runs and nodes (Using the PyTorch Compiler; Key Takeaways).
Use torch._dynamo.explain and TORCH_LOGS=+dynamo to find graph breaks (Profiling and Debugging Compiler Performance Issues).

Preallocate static buffers, keep graph structure fixed, capture the worst-case batch size for CUDA Graphs, and synchronise the capture stream before and after capture (Best Practices for CUDA Graphs).
Share one memory pool across batch-size-specialised CUDA graphs and capture largest first (Replaying the Graph, FireworksAI example).
Fix expert output buffer size and tune PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF to avoid fragmentation (Tuning the CUDA Memory Allocator).
Use activation checkpointing at transformer-block granularity and offload to CPU/NVMe with overlapped prefetch (memory sections).
Wrap FSDP per transformer block with use_orig_params=True when combining with torch.compile; use HYBRID_SHARD when the interconnect is decent but not fast (FSDP sections).
Use pin_memory, non_blocking, persistent_workers, prefetch_factor and a worker sweep (4, 8, 16, 32) in the DataLoader (Optimizing the Data Input Pipeline).
Use BF16 over FP16, TF32 for FP32 matmuls, and verify Tensor Core use in Nsight Compute (Key Takeaways).
Time GPU code with CUDA events, not time.time() (Key Takeaways).
Run a performance-regression CI job (TorchBench, GitHub Actions), pair throughput with accuracy checks, and watch PyTorch HUD (CI and HUD sections).

terms.definition: NVIDIA Tools Extension markers denote time ranges in a profiler timeline and let different profilers correlate events across the same phases.
Compiling a repeated block (e.g. a Transformer block) once and reusing that code across all occurrences, via torch.compiler.nested_compile_region().
Used by torch.compile mode=reduce-overhead to compile and cache separate static graphs for each input shape, sharing a memory pool across forward and backward captures.
GPU memory gets split into many noncontiguous free chunks over time, making it difficult to allocate a large tensor even if enough total memory remains free.
Recompute intermediate activations during the backward pass instead of storing them in the forward pass, trading compute for memory.
Fully Sharded Data Parallel, which shards model parameters, gradients and optimizer states across GPUs (ZeRO Stage-3).
Meta's open source tool that ingests PyTorch profiler traces from each rank and presents a unified timeline for multi-GPU diagnosis.
SuperOffload technique that performs speculative optimizer updates on the CPU while backprop runs on the GPU, then validates afterwards.
